baseline_models.focus_anchor: قال موسى لقومه اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ أنجاكم
baseline_models.mechanism: An uttered imperative addressed to a people makes recollection a collective speech-practice. The favor is specified as separation and escape, so the community repeatedly makes its extraction from Pharaoh's order present in language.

activation_trace.role: Uttered speech supplies the public vehicle by which the rescue-memory is voiced.
The human collective makes the command communal rather than an individual's private recollection.
Bringing something back into presence after absence supplies the act that keeps rescue operative.
Beneficent good condition identifies the remembered extraction as favor, not merely past motion.
Escape by separation gives the favor its operative shape: detachment from an enclosing regime.

changed_reading.before: Moses asks his people to recall God's past favor of rescue.
changed_reading.after: Moses institutes a collective counter-memory in which voicing the rescue repeatedly reasserts the people's separation from Pharaoh's order.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: يسومونكم سوء العذاب ويذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم
baseline_models.mechanism: The coordinated ongoing acts form a selective system: evil is imposed, sons as the line of descent are cut, while women are deliberately retained alive. The asymmetry makes the torment management of a population's continuity, not indiscriminate killing.

activation_trace.role: Imposing and assigning evil supplies the governing action that organizes the following harms.
Badness and degradation qualify the entire selective regime rather than only one violent act.
Cutting the throat supplies the literal lethal operation directed at the sons.
Sonship and descent make the victims bearers of communal continuity, not an undifferentiated age group.
Deliberately leaving alive supplies the contrasting nonlethal operation within the same torment system.
The collective of women identifies the population deliberately preserved under coercion.

changed_reading.before: Pharaoh's people tortured the Israelites by killing boys and sparing women.
changed_reading.after: The verse depicts demographic governance: a regime imposes degradation by cutting one channel of descent while retaining another population alive under its control.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم
baseline_models.mechanism: The demonstrative follows both imposed affliction and divine extraction. The split branch inventory sustains both an ordeal that exposes condition and a witnessed benefaction, while the Lord-root adds governance and formative completion; the phrase can gather the painful and saving sides without collapsing them.

activation_trace.role: Testing that makes a condition appear supplies the ordeal-side of the great event.
A fine deed made manifest supplies the benefaction-side of the same event-complex.
Nurturing, ordering, and bringing to completion make the event formative under lordly governance.
Magnitude and force enlarge the whole test-benefaction complex rather than one isolated detail.

changed_reading.before: The preceding oppression, or perhaps the rescue, was a great trial from the Lord.
changed_reading.after: The closing phrase can hold together an exposing ordeal and a manifested benefaction, leaving the demonstrative's scope productively open across affliction and extraction.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding commission joins bringing the people out with reminding them, and the surah's close joins public delivery with renewed recollection. The focus imperative therefore becomes a hinge through which a physical exodus is carried forward as an ongoing cognitive and verbal exodus.

activation_trace.role: A reminder that makes the event present anchors the focus command as an active mnemonic instrument.
Separation in rescue supplies the concrete movement that remembrance continues in another register.
Passage to the outside supplies the commissioned exodus immediately paired with reminder.
Making others remember explicitly couples Moses' mnemonic work to bringing his people out.
Delivery of a message extends the focus memory from one people into the surah's public communicative purpose.
Recollection at the close makes remembered presence the intended endpoint of public delivery.

structural_cues: 14:5 places Moses, his people, the darkness-to-light exit, and the command to remind immediately before the focus scene.
14:52 closes the whole surah with public delivery, warning, knowledge, and recollection.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated pairings of exit, reminder, and message-delivery. I supply the arrow that mnemonic re-presentation continues the exodus by moving people out of obscured understanding; a live alternative is that these are parallel duties without a causal link.

changed_reading.before: Remembering preserves the report of a completed rescue.
changed_reading.after: Remembering is one medium by which the rescue keeps happening: the event is brought out of absence and delivered as public guidance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The remembered favor enters a social feedback system. Recognition becomes gratitude and increase, whereas substituting disbelief for the same divine favor lodges a people in ruin. Memory is thus a safeguard on what communal leadership does with rescue.

activation_trace.role: Divine benefaction supplies the good condition whose later handling determines the people's trajectory.
Recognizing a favor and praising its giver supplies the positive response demanded of remembered rescue.
Increase and growth supply the stated consequence of grateful recognition.
The exact divine-favor lexeme returns as the object mishandled by those directing a people.
Putting one thing in another's place supplies the conversion of favor into disbelief.
Causing settlement in a place makes the leaders' handling of favor determine their people's habitat.
Ruin and corruption name the terminal social location produced by the substitution.

structural_cues: 14:7 immediately turns the focus remembrance into a gratitude-versus-disbelief conditional.
14:28 repeats نعمة الله and قوم while depicting leaders who convert favor and lodge their people in ruin.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the explicit gratitude/increase conditional and the later favor/substitution/settlement sequence. I supply the arrow that collective remembrance interrupts destructive leadership by stabilizing gratitude; a live alternative is that 14:28 addresses unrelated leaders and only offers an analogy.

changed_reading.before: The people should remember rescue because it was a divine favor.
changed_reading.after: They must remember so that a leader cannot socially convert rescue into ingratitude and carry the people back into a new abode of ruin.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus names one concrete favor in narrative detail, while 14:34 says the divine favor cannot be counted or exhaustively encompassed. The rescue becomes a graspable mnemonic index into an unbounded field of benefaction.

activation_trace.role: The concrete benefaction of extraction gives the people one narratable instance to hold.
The repeated benefaction lexeme expands the focus instance into the wider divine gift-field.
Enumerating countable items supplies the attempted operation that the favor exceeds.
Exhaustive numerical encompassing supplies the denied limit against which the named rescue functions as an index.

structural_cues: Both 14:6 and 14:34 use the singular expression نعمة الله, but only the focus unfolds one favor as a remembered story.
14:34 coordinates attempted counting with failure to encompass.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a concrete singular favor and a repeated singular favor that defeats enumeration. I supply the indexical arrow from the narrated rescue to a larger uncountable field; a live alternative is that the singular at 14:34 is simply collective and does not comment on the focus event's function.

changed_reading.before: The rescue is the particular favor the people are told to remember.
changed_reading.after: The rescue is a narratable handle on favor that cannot be exhausted by counting: one remembered event opens onto an immeasurable gift-field.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later oppressors offer messengers a coercive binary: expulsion from land or return into the dominant creed; divine reversal then settles them after the oppressors. Against that sequence, rescue from Pharaoh's آل is release from an order controlling both affiliation and place.

activation_trace.role: Escape by separation anchors deliverance as detachment from an enclosing relation.
A man's people who return to him supply the affiliation-system from which the rescued community is separated.
Forcing passage outside supplies the oppressors' spatial sanction against dissent.
Return after departure supplies the alternative demand of restored submission.
An adhered-to creed identifies what coerced return would reinstate.
Settlement and inhabitation supply the divine reversal of expulsion and forced affiliation.

structural_cues: 14:13 presents expulsion or return to the dominant creed as one coercive binary.
14:14 immediately reverses that binary by promising the threatened messengers settlement in the land after the wrongdoers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies escape from Pharaoh's آل and the later expulsion/return/creed/settlement sequence. I supply the arrow that آل functions as an affiliation-order controlling habitat as well as a household; a live alternative keeps the focus rescue primarily physical and آل primarily familial.

changed_reading.before: God physically rescued the people from Pharaoh's household and its violence.
changed_reading.after: God extracted them from coerced belonging itself: a regime that could dictate where they lived and to which order they must return.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah later depicts punishment in which death arrives from every place yet the sufferer does not die, then contrasts enduring life whose greeting is peace. That split sharpens the focus's deliberate keeping-alive: biological continuation inside an imposed torment is not mercy and can itself be calibrated domination.

activation_trace.role: Deliberate preservation from killing anchors the ambiguous survival of the women inside the torment clause.
Imposed evil keeps that preservation under the governing category of coercive harm.
Loss of life arriving without completed death supplies the model of prolonged non-death within punishment.
Painful punishment explicitly frames the scene in which death is approached but withheld.
Stable abiding not quickly touched by extinction supplies the positive form of continued life.
Greeting as a wish of life and safety gives preservation its relationally positive quality.
Safety from harm distinguishes fulfilled life from mere biological non-killing.

structural_cues: 14:17 coordinates death coming from every place with the explicit negation of being dead, all inside punishment.
14:23 coordinates enduring residence, a life-greeting, and safety.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies non-death within punishment and, separately, abiding life marked by peace. I supply the contrastive arrow that the focus's kept-alive women occupy the first semantic pole unless safety is supplied; live alternatives include forced labor, reproductive control, humiliation, or simple selective sparing, none of which the packet resolves.

changed_reading.before: The women are spared from the lethal policy applied to the sons.
changed_reading.after: Their bare survival is part of the torment's design, not evidence of mercy: life withheld from death can remain coercive until it is joined to safety and peace.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah's tyrant, weak followers, arrogant superiors, and contested authority expose a layered dependency order. This activates Pharaoh's آل as a regime of return and allegiance whose coercive power transmits bodily exposure downward.

activation_trace.role: People who return to a man and to whom he returns supply a relational household larger than mere co-residence.
Coercive assignment of evil supplies the downward operation of that household-regime.
Compulsion and coercion identify the tyrant's characteristic mode of rule.
Lack of power supplies the exposed lower stratum that seeks relief from its superiors.
Arrogant self-magnification supplies the posture of the dominant stratum.
Allegiance and successive following supply the relation binding the weak to the arrogant.
Power and governing authority supply the category whose presence or absence determines coercive responsibility.

structural_cues: 14:21 stages weak followers asking arrogant leaders to absorb some punishment, but the leaders cannot.
14:22 distinguishes claimed influence from actual coercive authority and returns responsibility to respondents.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies آل as reciprocal affiliation, imposed evil, a coercive tyrant, and a follower/superior hierarchy. I supply the arrow that Pharaoh's آل names a political dependency network through which harm is administered; a live alternative limits آل to kin and officials without importing the later hierarchy.

changed_reading.before: Pharaoh's household is the collective agent that tortured the people.
changed_reading.after: Pharaoh's آل can be read as a layered dependency regime: allegiance concentrates authority above while imposed bodily risk is transmitted to the weak below.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it transfers the good-word tree's root-and-branch architecture into genealogy. It remains anchored in أبناء via the focus branch of sonship and descent, the repeated بني, and the later ذرية image of small things spreading. Downstream prose should call it a possible cross-domain activation, not claim that the tree parable directly glosses Pharaoh's policy.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: يذبحون أبناءكم: sons as بنوة and a line attributed to an origin

activation_trace.role: Literal throat-cutting supplies the operation that removes the line's young bearers.
Sonship, descent, and attribution to an origin supply the genealogical anchor for future branching.
The base or root supplies the stable origin from which continuity can grow.
Branching out from an origin supplies the cross-domain image for extending descent.
Pulling a thing out wholly from its root supplies the counter-image of terminated continuity.
The later speaker's own sons reactivate descent as a protected future tied to worship.
Small particles spreading supply an exploratory material image for offspring dispersed forward.

changed_reading.before: The regime kills male children as one especially cruel component of persecution.
changed_reading.after: The selective killing can be heard as anti-branching: an attempt to uproot a people's future extension while retaining present bodies under rule.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the closing bound-and-covered criminals are not explicitly identified with Pharaoh's people. It remains anchored in the focus's imposed bodily punishment and the closing sequence's equally material binding, clothing, and covering. Render it only as a possible formal reversal in which bodily subjection is reassigned, not as an asserted direct referent.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: يسومونكم سوء العذاب ويذبحون: imposed punishment enacted on bodies

activation_trace.role: The imposed assignment of evil anchors the original direction of bodily subjection.
Pain and punishment supply the juridical-affective field shared with the closing images.
Joining and binding things together supplies the criminals' constrained bodily arrangement.
Tight fastening in fetters makes coercion materially return upon criminal bodies.
A garment worn on the body supplies the enclosing medium of the reassigned punishment.
Viscous pitch supplies the material coating that turns clothing into torment.
A cover rising over and concealing the thing completes the reversal as total bodily envelopment.

changed_reading.before: The focus remembers escape from a regime that imposed bodily punishment.
changed_reading.after: The memory may also carry an anticipatory reversal: those associated with crime become the bound, clothed, and covered objects of bodily subjection.

strongest_changes: Remembering becomes a public exodus-medium and a gratitude-bearing social practice, not passive recall.
Pharaoh's torment becomes demographic and political governance: forced belonging, selective survival, and pressure on lineage.
The later contrast between non-death inside punishment and abiding life with peace shows that being kept alive is not equivalent to mercy.
The repeated divine-favor formula makes the focus rescue both a communal feedback pivot and a concrete index of uncountable benefaction.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet repeatedly reactivated exact focus constructions: exit, return, and settlement around أنجاكم and آل; gratitude, substitution, and failed enumeration around نعمة; and death-without-dying versus peaceful abiding around يستحيون.
remaining_uncertainties: The scope of ذلكم and the balance between ordeal and benefaction in بلاء remain genuinely open.
The packet does not settle whether preserving the women served labor, reproductive control, humiliation, or another coercive purpose.
Reading آل as a political dependency regime extends, but does not erase, its ordinary household sense.
The genealogy/tree activation and the final bodily reversal are formal echoes and should remain exploratory.
